descriptionChirho: The inherent character, constitution, or essential quality of something; the way things are by their created order. Used of the natural function of sexual relations (Rom 1:26 'natural use'), the nature of deity (Gal 4:8 'not by nature gods'), human nature shared universally (Jas 3:7 'every kind of nature is tamed'), the divine nature believers partake of (2 Pet 1:4), and natural instinct (Rom 2:14 'do by nature the things of the law'). Spanish 'naturaleza', Arabic 'الطَّبيعة', Korean '본성', Swahili 'asili', Hindi 'स्वभाव' all denote inherent character.

An adverbial/instrumental use of physis in the dative case meaning 'from birth' or 'innately', indicating a condition that is natural or inborn rather than acquired; used of Gentiles who are uncircumcised 'by nature' (Rom 2:27), Jews who are Jews 'by nature' (Gal 2:15), humanity 'by nature children of wrath' (Eph 2:3), and things done 'by nature' without law (Rom 2:14). Spanish 'por naturaleza', Arabic 'بِالطَّبيعة', Korean '본성으로', Swahili 'kwa asili', Hindi 'स्वभाव से' all consistently render the instrumental/adverbial meaning.
